notes.title: Future Improvements to Archetype Balancing and the Doll System
notes.notes: [p]First of all, we want to sincerely thank you for supporting [i]Cubic Cosmos[/i]. Since launch, we've received far more feedback and suggestions than we ever expected. We know the game is far from perfect in its current state, yet so many of you have chosen to encourage us and share your honest thoughts. Seeing your passion has been both moving and inspiring, and it strengthens our determination to keep polishing the game.[/p][p]Among the feedback we've received, two topics stand out as the most frequently mentioned: [b]archetype balance[/b] and [b]the Doll system[/b]. We'd like to share some of our current thoughts and the direction we plan to take moving forward.[/p][p][/p][h3]Archetype Balance[/h3][p]Archetype balance is something many of you care deeply about. We understand that some archetypes feel too strong, too weak, or too difficult to make work.[/p][p]Here's how we're approaching it:[/p][p]We don't intend to take the conventional route of nerfing whatever's strong until everything feels the same.[/p][p]We know nerf-heavy balancing can feel extremely frustrating. We want to preserve a sense of fun and power.[/p][p]When it comes to adjusting cards, Relics, and hero skills, we'll be careful and deliberate.[/p][p]Our priority will be to improve the cards and items that currently see little to no use—whether that means buffing their attributes or fully reworking them—so they become exciting, viable options.[/p][p]Our vision of ideal balance is one where every card and item has a role to play within its archetype, making it easier for different builds to come together and shine across the game's many modes.[/p][p]Once the most critical bugs have been resolved, we'll begin working on new content while also gradually rolling out balance improvements.[/p][p]If at any point we make a change that feels like a step backward, please don't hesitate to let us know—whether that's in the Steam forums or by joining our [url="https://discord.gg/AeJjkNZdYc"]Discord[/url] and telling us directly.[/p][p]For us, progress comes from open communication.[/p][p][/p][h3]Doll System[/h3][p]We've also noticed that high-score Dolls feel somewhat awkward in the current game. If they appear early in a run, they can make encounters far too easy; if they appear later, they often feel underwhelming.[/p][p]To address this, we're planning to expand the way Dolls work in future updates. Our current idea is to allow players to bring multiple Dolls at the start of a run so that they can enjoy the thrill of using a high-scoring Doll.[/p][p]Our goal is for Dolls across all score levels—from low to high—to each have meaningful and enjoyable roles to play.[/p][p][/p][p]Once again, thank you all for your continued support and feedback![/p][p]Please keep on sharing your experiences and ideas with us, and together we'll make Cubic Cosmos even better.[/p]

notes.title: Steam Cloud Save Issues
notes.notes: [p]Hail, Cosmonauts![/p][p]A number of players have recently reported that Steam Cloud saves have been failing.[/p][p]Currently, no game seems to have an optimal solution for this issue, which most commonly occurs when switching between different devices. Please see below for some suggested fixes which we hope will help you to prevent save loss and restore your saves.[/p][p][/p][h3]How to Restore Your Saves[/h3][olist][*][p]When you encounter the issue, [b]do not quit the game.[/b][/p][/*][*][p]Download your cloud save files.[/p][p]Log in to your Steam account, then on the Steam homepage click “Help” → “Steam Support” → “My Account” → “Data Related to Your Steam Account.” Scroll down to “Uploaded Content” and find “Steam Cloud.”[/p][/*][*][p]Overwrite and verify your saves.[/p][p]Exit the game and overwrite your local save file with the cloud save file, then restart the game.[/p][p]If your in-game progress is as expected, the issue has been resolved. If not, then carry on to the next step."[/p][/*][*][p]Access the device with the latest save.[/p][p]Make a backup of the save file on the device with the newest save, then switch Steam to offline mode to prevent the local save from being overwritten.[/p][p]Enter the game and confirm that your game progress is as expected, then exit the game and switch Steam back to online mode.[/p][p]When Steam notifies you of a conflict between local and cloud saves, choose to save the local file to the cloud. This should fix the issue.[/p][/*][/olist][p][/p][h3]How to Avoid This Issue[/h3][olist][*][p]After exiting the game, make sure your Steam Cloud saves are synced before quitting Steam.[/p][/*][*][p]Periodically restart Steam to trigger cloud save checks. Avoid leaving Steam idle for long periods of time, which can lead to inconsistencies.[/p][/*][*][p]We suggest making manual backups of important save files.[/p][/*][/olist][p][/p][p]We have also added a few precautionary measures as part of today's v0.13.32 update.[/p][p]Thank you for your patience as we work to resolve this issue.[/p]

notes.title: Share Your Greatest Triumphs in the Cosmos Highlights Feature!
notes.notes: [p]Since the release of Cubic Cosmos, we've received a ton of support and encouragement from players. Thank you to everyone who purchased the game, wrote reviews, and shared your experiences! Your enthusiasm and feedback drive us to continue improving the game.[/p][p][/p][p]To thank our players old and new, we're starting a regular feature we're calling [b]Cosmos Highlights[/b]![/p][quote][p]Feature: Cosmos Highlights[/p][p]Content: We'll regularly collect submission from players across multiple platforms, featuring your coolest and most skillful victories on the battlefield.[/p][p]We'll highlight 5-10 awesome battles and include their battle codes.[/p][p]Use the battle codes to experience the incredible scenes for yourself![/p][/quote][p][/p][p][b]🎮Share Your Best Battles With Battle Codes![/b][/p][p]"Whether you're taking down bosses with a basic starter deck, chaining together huge combos, or buffing a pawn until it's a one-shot killer...[/p][p]Don't forget to copy down your battle code so you can share your sickest moves![/p][p][/p][p][b]How to Participate[/b]: Post screenshots or videos of your best battles on Steam, X, Youtube or Tiktok and include your battle code, a short description of the battle (e.g. "incredible comeback", "one-shot kill", or "mega combo"), and the hashtag #CubicCosmos.[/p][p][/p][p]✨We'll be selecting submissions that get the most likes or generate the most buzz for our first Cosmos Highlights feature! The feature will be updated periodically in future, so you'll have more chances to get involved![/p]

notes.title: Cubic Cosmos Is Now in Steam Early Access!

notes.title: Cubic Cosmos Playtest has concluded
notes.notes: [p]From the bottom of our hearts, we'd like to thank the Cubic Cosmos community for your ongoing interest, support and feedback, which has been invaluable to us.[/p][p]After two months of polishing, a new version of Cubic Cosmos will be available soon, packed to the gills with new content! notes.title: Dev Log #02 | From Next Fest to Early Access: Our Plan
notes.notes: [p]Hail, Cosmonauts![/p][p]Since Next Fest, we've received a ton of feedback from players—not just praise, but also suggestions that have given us lots to consider. Thank you to everyone for supporting Cubic Cosmos![/p][p][/p][p]During this time, we've continued to update and improve the demo while also sorting out content for the Early Access version.[/p][p]In accordance with our original plan, we've arrived at a version that we're satisfied with in terms of playability and experience.[/p][p]But we don't want to settle for "satisfied"; we want the Early Access version to have that "one-more-turn" quality that keeps players coming back for more. That's why we've decided to further expand and polish the game so we can create a version with even better pacing and content.[/p][p][/p][h2]What Will Be In The Early Access Version?[/h2][olist][*][p][b]More Cards and Classes[/b][/p][p]The three main classes are being further polished. At time of release we plan to have 10 heroes and over 200 cards available.[/p][/*][*][p][b]More Gameplay Modes[/b][/p][p]Gameplay Mode 1: Tutorial + fixed boss chapters + multiple higher difficulty random boss chapters.[/p][p]Gameplay Mode 2: Daily challenges.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Mastery Mode[/b][/p][p]Similar to an "endless mode", Mastery Mode will be available upon completing a run.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Controller Support[/b][/p][p]Support for Steam Deck and gamepads.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Achievements[/b][/p][p]Base achievements, challenge achievements and exploration achievements.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Doll System[/b][/p][p]Major improvements and new features for the Doll system.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Improved UI, Sound Effects, Animations[/b][/p][p]Thank you to everyone who made us aware of issues they experienced during the demo. We're working to update the UI and improve sound effects and animations.[/p][/*][*][p][b]More Detailed Interactions[/b][/p][/*][/olist][p]This chart should help everyone understand the differences between each version. As you can see, the new version doesn't just mean more content, but a more complete game overall.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45444613/e7ba8d031d181c5e550e9d5c8b6d964f6133d5f2.png"][/img][/p][h2]Demo Still Available[/h2][p]We're now working flat out on the new version of the game. notes.notes:

Hail, Cosmonauts!
The Cubic Cosmos demo has now been online for one week! Thank you for playing, and thanks for your feedback and suggestions, which have helped us to uncover many issues and make a number of improvements. Over the past few days, we've continued to release fixes to improve your gaming experience.
[b]The current demo will be available until May 6[/b]. If you haven't experienced Cubic Cosmos yet, now's your chance—and please feel free to provide your feedback and suggestions!

[b]The next demo will be released as part of June's Steam Next Fest[/b], and will include a major update to the game. The current plan is as follows:

2. Improving stage pacing and deckbuilding experience, increasing strategic depth and enjoyment.
3. Fully implementing finished art assets and replacing all placeholder cards.
4. Differentiating the gameplay experience for different heroes.
5. Improving the Doll system to make obtaining and using Dolls more convenient.
6. Improving interactions for more intuitive gameplay and a smoother experience.
7. Complete overhaul and upgrade of sound effects.

We're working hard to polish the game, and we hope you'll enjoy a more complete and even more fun version of Cubic Cosmos as part of Steam Next Fest!
If you've liked the game so far, don't forget to add Cubic Cosmos to your wishlist. You'll be notified as soon as the Next Fest demo is available!

notes.title: Cubic Cosmos Demo Coming Soon!
notes.notes:
Hail, future Cosmonauts! We're Inkstone Atelier, an independent game studio based in Chengdu, China.
Back in 2023, we released our first game, Looper Tactics. It's a game that left us with mixed feelings; it failed to recoup its costs, but we were delighted to see the positive reception it got. It's that support from our players—which has always been the most important thing to us—that has kept us making games.
Not long after, while working on our second game, we caught a lucky break. Looper Tactics caught the attention of Lilith Games, and they offered to support us. With renewed confidence and more resources than ever before, we knuckled down and dedicated all of 2024 to working on our new title: Cubic Cosmos.

After over a year of hard work, [b]Cubic Cosmos will debut its first demo as part of Eastern Game Fest[/b]. We're pretty nervous, but also extremely excited to see what you think of it.

We wanted to write a devlog to share our development journey and our design philosophy. If you have anything to say about the gameplay, setting, or anything else we share, we'd love to discuss it with you! You can leave your thoughts in the comments or join our [url=https://discord.gg/M8GhQ9Cajs]official Discord[/url].

[h3]What Kind of Game Do We Want to Make?[/h3]
Cubic Cosmos is a strategic roguelike deckbuilder. In a crowded genre, we know that innovation is what'll make or break this game. Most deckbuilders on the market right now are modeled after Hearthstone or Slay the Spire—we want to break out of that framework.
In the early stages of the project, we focused on what new ideas we could bring to the table. We settled on what we're calling "falling card combat". Kind of like Tetris, but with slavering monsters coming at you instead of tetrominoes. We wanted a game that was easy to jump into, but also had enough depth and progression elements to reward players who synergized and strategized.
Our previous game mostly centered on buffing your minion cards as much as possible and slugging it out with your enemy. With Cubic Cosmos, we've added tons of new effects and mechanics, unlocking a huge variety of new playstyles and making every run unique.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45444613/ea5cc698b7391bf5502957058d76d57ee3ccbbe2.png[/img]

[h3]Old Tricks, New Art[/h3]
There's an old adage here in China, one that most indie game devs will probably agree with: Poverty breeds innovation. Even with our limited resources, we've always tried to improve our visuals in clever ways.
During a visit to the Sichuan Museum, we were struck by their collection of Han dynasty "portrait bricks". It got us thinking: Why do cards need to be "flat"? With that in mind, we tried using traditional art techniques to give our 2D card art more depth and dimensionality. These 2D models are placed on separate "background plates". When a card attacks, its 2D model separates from its background plate and pops out, then rams into its target with a satisfying impact.
The few folks who have tested the game thus far have said they really liked the feeling of blowing up enemies, which counts as a success in our books. It's a bit of ingenuity to get around limited resources, but we're happy with the results... unless one of you wants to give us 100 million dollars, in which case we'll do 3D models for every card (kidding but also not really kidding).
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45444613/504dcef46aa62d949ca0c5865aef916c469f61ec.png[/img]

[h3]Development Progress[/h3]
During the development of our last game, mostly due to our lack of experience, we frequently encountered fundamental architectural problems. We lost a lot of valuable time changing and fixing things we already thought were settled. 
Here's another colorful Chinese adage for you: Every pit you fall into is a lesson learned (it sounds snappier in Chinese, honest). We're happy to inform you that development is going a lot smoother this time around. With our improved devtools and processes, we've saved a lot of time that we can spend on design and debugging.
As for the visual side of things, our artists have been hard at work. We've already got a whole gallery's worth of card art, running the gamut from cool to beautiful to adorable. We can't wait for you to see it all!
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45444613/b66464e5018397000e7a03592317ee39b5c1f38c.png[/img]

[h3]Demo Coming Soon[/h3]
We're hard at work putting the finishing touches on the first demo for Cubic Cosmos. If all goes to plan, you'll be able to play the demo next week.
If you're interested in our game, don't forget to add Cubic Cosmos to your Wishlist, and please feel free to leave any feedback and suggestions you have once you've played the demo. Thanks for your support, and we'll see you soon!
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45444613/05e08d73ccbf975881674030fea76092053afe50.png[/img]
